# App and GTK theming

The palette rules and generated files are in `CLAUDE.md` (Theme). This covers the apps outside Quickshell.

## App themes (generated by `apply.py`, templates in `quickshell/theme/templates/`)
- VSCodium and Zen follow the active theme (cherry, dusty, ... or `wallpaper`). Neovim isn't installed and Steam would need Millennium (patches the client): skipped. Vesktop was tried (a generated CSS theme) and dropped: it looked ugly and Discord's CSS variables are hard to pin down. Spotify was tried (a generated Spicetify theme) and dropped: a pastel palette on Spotify looked awful; Spotify stays on whatever theme you picked in Spicetify (Marketplace). All of it is a best guess until tried live.
- One-time setup you do yourself: **VSCodium** (works, confirmed live): restart it, then Ctrl+K Ctrl+T > "Retro (quickshell)" (a hand-placed extension folder in `~/.vscode-oss/extensions`). It does not follow a theme switch by itself: after switching, run "Developer: Reload Window" in VSCodium. **Zen**: add `@import "<home>/.config/zen-qs/theme.css";` to the profile's `chrome/userChrome.css` and set `toolkit.legacyUserProfileCustomizations.stylesheets` to true in about:config (the `--zen-*` names are guesses; plain Firefox variables come first). Nothing is ever written into the Zen profile.
- `apply.py` skips an app whose folder doesn't exist (`OUTPUTS` third item); editor syntax colours are derived roles (`syn_*`, 4.5:1 on the lightest background).

## GTK theme (`theme/gtkgen.py`, called by `apply.py`)
- ClassicPlatinumStreamlined and RetroismIcons (linux-retroism, MIT) are vendored unmodified in `themes/` and `icons/` (licence `themes/LICENSE-linux-retroism`, upstream commit in install.sh `RETROISM_REV`; never edit them); `install.sh` copies them to `~/.local/share` only when missing. ClassicPlatinumStreamlined is recoloured into a new folder `~/.local/share/themes/QsRetro` on every theme change and at Quickshell start. The installed original is only read. Greys map to a ramp (outline, dark, shadow, base, paper; paper = the base mixed 90% towards white, so content areas read as white against the tinted chrome), the blue selection colour to `select_bar` (its text: `select_text`), `color: #000` to `text`; red / orange / green stay. The small PNG assets (arrows, check boxes, sliders) are recoloured the same way. Icons: `theme/icongen.py` rotates the blue family (hue 180-260) of `~/.local/share/icons/RetroismIcons` onto the accent's hue into `QsRetroIcons` (lightness / saturation kept; reds, greens, greys untouched; `Inherits=RetroismIcons`; only the 552 real PNGs are processed, the 1,945 links are copied as links). `gtk-icon-theme-name`, xsettingsd and `install.sh` use `QsRetroIcons`; Quickshell's own icons (`shell.qml` pragma) stay on `RetroismIcons` so a missing generated theme can't blank the bar. `gtk-3.0/settings.ini`, `gtk-4.0/settings.ini` and `xsettingsd.conf` name the theme `QsRetro`; `~/.config/gtk-4.0/gtk.css` and `assets` are links into it (apply.py only replaces a link that points into one of the two themes, never a real file).
- A changed theme is re-read by running GTK apps only after the theme name flips: `apply.py` does `gsettings set ... gtk-theme Adwaita`, then back to `QsRetro`, and the same for `icon-theme` via `hicolor` (each only when the generated one is the current gsettings value). `install.sh` sets `gtk-theme`, `icon-theme` and `font-hinting full` through gsettings (asks first). Qt has no config at all and is not themed.
- Testing: run `apply.py <theme> --no-reload` with a scratch HOME and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`; without `--no-reload` it does `pkill -USR1 kitty` and `hyprctl reload` on the live session. The generated CSS was checked with GTK 3's own `Gtk.CssProvider` (0 errors on every palette); GTK 4's CSS was only compared with the original's messages.
